chapter: Back in New York: Heard and Dizzy
title: Detroit debut with Dizzy while Louis Armstrong's sextet was in town
summary: His first job with Dizzy coincided with Louis Armstrong and Earl Hines in town and radio exchanges between bebop and older jazz.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So you started working there in Detroit, your first job with the Dizzy Gillespie Band.

Yeah! That was quite an experience because in the atmosphere...Louis (Armstrong) was there too. He was...just formed his new sextet with Jack Teagarden and Earl Hines and Arvell Shaw and I think it was Zutty (Singleton) on drums. And one day Dizzy'd be on the radio and said, "We got the new music," and then another day Louis'd be on and say, "Well look, Bebop ain't this..." And I was confused, "What they doin'?," on the radio, you know. But I'm sure that they loved each other, you know what I mean, shoot. But that was a little strange to me, at the time.
